$schema_note: LUMI design tokens v0.1.518 (2026-08-16). Mirrors tokens/lumi-theme.css; usage in references/design-rules.md. Version lockstep: tokens carry the skill version. Repository language: English only (red line).

dark.note: applied only on explicit user request, via one body.dark override block — never a forked file

palette.note: one structure, two palettes. v0.1.340: the light canvas is pure white, not the warm cream the field has settled on, and the dark canvas is Apple space grey. The state palette grew by two with fixed meanings: amber = partial, in progress, awaiting an input; brass = reference, archival, out of scope but real. Before this, partial and not-built both rendered as dashed grey, so a deck could not say the one thing it most needed to say about itself. Every semantic colour clears 4.5:1 as text on its own canvas. v0.1.345: the light ramp. Five discrete steps from the accent toward the canvas, for fields and surfaces only — it carries no meaning. One colour one meaning still governs data. Every step carries text on both canvases; on-light-ramp-5 is the foreground for step 5 and on-light-ramp-low for steps 4 down to 1. v0.1.346: --lime is a surface colour, not a member of the text ladder. On the light canvas it measures 1.21:1 as text and may only be a fill with --on-lime reversed out of it (16.44:1); on the dark canvas it is the accent at 13.90:1. It carries no meaning.

contrast.note: WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance ratios, recomputed by scripts/check/check_design.py (D1). Recompute and update this block whenever a palette value moves; the numbers are the reason the alphas are what they are.

chart.note: CVD-validated triple; on dark canvas use the lifted forms from palette.dark

font.note: v1.2+: D-DIN is the single Latin face (titles ALL-CAPS weight 700, tight leading — the register comes from weight and scale, not tracking; 400-uppercase-tracked reads as a spec sheet, per the comment beside --w-display; CJK titles: weight 700 + 0.04em tracking, no uppercase). SIL OFL (Datto 2017), Latin-only; vendored in assets/fonts/ and embedded by scripts/build/embed_font.py. tabular-nums always on for data.

display_title.weight_note: said 400 through 0.1.442 while the CSS shipped --w-display: 700 with a comment naming 400-uppercase as the exact mistake — the JSON restated the mistake as the rule for over a hundred releases

typography.note: v0.1.338 raised the chart scale. The old scale (11 / 10.5 / 9.5) contradicted design-rules.md prose (14 / 10-11 / 11); tokens win per CLAUDE.md, so deliverables shipped 9.5px source lines. v0.1.352: `size_floor_px` renamed to `size_smallest_px` (CSS `--fs-fine`), and the claim that it 'binds every text run' is withdrawn — it never should have survived 0.1.340, which withdrew the 11px floor as invented without an ask. THERE IS NO TYPE FLOOR. This value records the smallest size the scale actually uses; it is not a limit, and design-rules.md 1 is the authority that says so. Because CLAUDE.md makes tokens win on conflict, a floor asserted here silently overrode the prose in every deliverable built from this file for twelve releases.

retired.name: D7 page-fill floor
retired.note: measured the bounding box of all ink, so a small chart with a long caption scored as full, and it was satisfiable by stretching table rows while four diagrams rendered at 40% of their cell

retired.name: universal type floor
retired.note: invented without an ask; the value survives as size_smallest_px, which records the smallest size in use and binds nothing

retired_note: v0.1.353. A withdrawn number is a fact the authority has to state, or no check can tell 'withdrawn' from 'deleted by accident' — and a withdrawn floor that survives in a prose copy is this repository's documented worst drift: the 82% fill floor and the 11px type floor both outlived their withdrawal by four versions in two entry points nobody was checking. scripts/check/check_repo.py reads this register and requires every restatement of these values to carry a withdrawal marker in the same sentence. Each entry carries a `context` list because a bare number is not a rule: '40%' names the withdrawn D9 share cap in one sentence and 'four diagrams rendered at 40% of their cell' in another, and those are opposite claims written with the same digits. A value counts as a restatement only when the paragraph also carries one of its context phrases.

assets.icons: assets/icons/ — the eight semantic icons named in design-rules.md §6, hairline 1.25px, stroke=currentColor, 24x24
assets.vectors: assets/vectors/ — globe-orthographic.svg and world-flat.svg, original geometry
assets.note: v0.1.338. A rule may not mandate an asset the package does not ship: §5 required a semantic icon library for six versions and shipped none, so deliverables carried zero icons, and the cover rule banned imagery because there was no photo library rather than shipping vector geography that needs none.

layout.tier1_callouts: at most 1 per page, and no more than a third of a deck's pages
layout.footer: source line + page number as N / total
layout.verification_matrix: language x viewport (design / print / short-laptop); footer visible at every point

region.space: oklch, converted to sRGB hex on emit
region.note: v0.1.387. Hue encodes region IDENTITY here and carries no data meaning, the standing light_ramp already has; one colour one meaning still governs data. Owner directive, and two proposals were rejected on the way: an 8-hue ceiling (the map layer needs more regions) and a delta-E floor of 20 over ALL pairs, which is unsatisfiable at every N — the best achievable is 18.1 at N=8 and 6.8 at N=20. The floor binds adjacent pairs only. A four-band construction was built and then withdrawn: it satisfied the adjacent floor while putting three of eleven regions inside one narrow window, so Europe and Southeast Asia measured 5.0 apart and rendered as one colour. Even spacing with a max-separation assignment gives 12.0 over all pairs and needs no constraint on the registry. Values are hex, never oklch(): parse_color in check_design.py cannot read that form and D1 would skip every region hue in silence.
